title: Constraints-aware Adaptive Routing with Hybrid Waveguides for Photonic Integrated Circuits
problem: Automatic optical routing for photonic integrated circuits (PICs) typically assumes uniform waveguide types, neglecting real-world requirements for multiple waveguide types to enhance performance and integration density. Prior work lacks support for hybrid waveguide routing with stringent constraints.
motivation: PICs offer superior bandwidth and energy efficiency for next-generation computing and interconnects, but effective design automation supporting diverse waveguide types and matching constraints is needed.
method: Proposes an adaptive waveguide routing framework with two components: (1) fast initial routing algorithm optimizing waveguide paths considering target net lengths, length matching constraints, bend minimization, and hybrid waveguide compatibility, and (2) MILP-based automatic transition insertion technique strategically deploying different waveguide types to reduce transmission loss while satisfying matching constraints.
key_novelty: First framework for automatic optical routing supporting hybrid waveguide classes with both length-matching and loss-minimization constraints using MILP optimization.
contributions: Adaptive initial routing algorithm handling multiple waveguide types and diverse constraints
MILP-based transition insertion for waveguide type selection and loss minimization
Up to 37% reduction in total insertion loss on target-length routing and 5-14% improvement in multi-net cases
limitations: Evaluation limited to specific PIC designs; scalability to very large photonic circuits not discussed; computational complexity of MILP transitions not characterized.
primary_theme: Hybrid waveguide routing for photonic integrated circuits
